scheme_name: PMMSY: Inputs for Saline /Alkaline Water Aquaculture - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana or PMMSY is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about the holistic development of the fisheries sector in India. 

It is particularly focused on increasing fish production and productivity. 

The PMMSY scheme has a special component dedicated to saline and alkaline water aquaculture. 

This component is crucial for states like Haryana, which have specific challenges and opportunities in aquaculture. 

The primary objective of the PMMSY is to enhance fish production to 220 lakh metric tonnes by the year 2024-25. 

It also aims to increase the income of fishers and fish farmers by providing them with necessary inputs and support. 

The scheme is designed to create a sustainable and responsible aquaculture sector. 

The PMMSY aims to enhance the livelihoods of around 28 million people who depend on fisheries. 

The scheme has a financial outlay of ₹20,050 crore over a period of five years. 

Of this amount, ₹9,407 crore is allocated for the development of inland fisheries and aquaculture. 

The remaining funds are earmarked for marine fisheries and other related activities. 

The specific benefits under the PMMSY for saline and alkaline water aquaculture include financial assistance for setting up aquaculture farms. 

Farmers can receive up to 40% of the project cost as a subsidy. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, this subsidy can go up to 60%. 

The maximum project cost eligible for assistance is ₹20 lakh. 

This means that a farmer could receive a subsidy of up to ₹8 lakh for a project costing ₹20 lakh. 

The scheme also provides assistance for the establishment of hatcheries, feed mills, and other necessary infrastructure. 

Farmers can also receive training and capacity-building support under this scheme. 

The eligibility criteria for availing benefits under the PMMSY include being a registered fish farmer or fisher. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old. 

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants. 

Income criteria are not explicitly defined but priority is given to small and marginal farmers. 

Applicants must also demonstrate the technical capability to manage aquaculture operations. 

The application process for PMMSY involves several steps. 

First, interested applicants must approach the local fisheries department in Haryana. 

They need to fill out an application form that can be obtained from the department. 

The application must include details about the proposed project, including location and expected output. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and proof of land ownership or lease. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the fisheries department. 

The department may conduct a site visit to assess the feasibility of the project. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is released upon project approval. 

Subsequent installments are released upon verification of progress. 

The PMMSY scheme is implemented through the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The department has a dedicated helpline for queries related to the scheme. 

The contact number for the Department of Fisheries in Haryana is +91-171-274-2500. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in aquaculture. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt eco-friendly methods to minimize environmental impact. 

The scheme promotes the use of quality seeds and feed to enhance productivity. 

It also aims to reduce the dependency on wild fish stocks by promoting aquaculture. 

The PMMSY has set a target to create 68 lakh direct jobs in the fisheries sector by 2024-25. 

This includes jobs in aquaculture, processing, and marketing. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the contribution of the fisheries sector to the Gross Value Added (GVA) of the agriculture sector. 

The target is to increase the GVA of fisheries to ₹1,00,000 crore by 2024-25. 

The PMMSY is part of the broader vision of the Government of India to achieve self-sufficiency in fish production. 

It aligns with the National Fisheries Policy which aims to promote sustainable fisheries management. 

The scheme also addresses the nutritional security of the population by promoting fish consumption. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

The PMMSY encourages the establishment of fish markets and processing units. 

This is aimed at enhancing the value chain in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme also supports research and development in aquaculture practices. 

It aims to introduce innovative technologies to improve fish farming. 

The PMMSY is expected to significantly boost the aquaculture sector in Haryana. 

It provides a comprehensive framework for the development of saline and alkaline water aquaculture. 

Farmers are encouraged to diversify their income sources through aquaculture. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the livelihoods of many families in Haryana. 

It is a significant step towards achieving sustainable development in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is a testament to the commitment of the Government of India towards enhancing the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in rural economies by generating employment and income. 

The PMMSY is a vital initiative that reflects the importance of fisheries in India's agricultural landscape. 

It aims to empower fishers and fish farmers with the necessary tools and resources. 

The scheme is a crucial part of India's strategy to enhance food security and promote sustainable livelihoods. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges faced by the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a resilient and productive aquaculture ecosystem in Haryana. 

The scheme is a significant opportunity for farmers to improve their economic conditions. 

The PMMSY is poised to make a lasting impact on the fisheries sector in India.
